title: 20-Layer Asymmetric FP with ±15nm Bounded Perturbation and Curvature Penalty
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining layers 8-19 to ±15nm perturbation bounds while preserving the high-performing layers 1-8 baseline (158.5/268.4 nm quarter-wave) will recover the 0.92+ target score by preventing optimizer-induced resonance destruction while allowing sufficient local refinement of the asymmetric cavity region.
design_principle: Hybrid optimization: freeze proven high-performance mirror section, apply bounded perturbation with curvature regularization to cavity section. Based on defective DBR principle where cavity layers determine transmission peak characteristics while mirror layers establish stopband foundation.
proposed_topology: 20 explicit layers: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate. Layers 1-8 fixed at iteration 02 baseline; layers 9-20 optimized within ±15nm of mean thickness from iterations 13, 17, and 06.
soft_objectives: maintain thickness continuity between adjacent layers
manufacturing_considerations: ±15nm bounds compatible with standard deposition monitoring
alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 sequence simplifies process control
theory_basis: Defective DBR bandpass filter principle: (HL)^N D(LH)^N structure creates transmission resonance
Quarter-wave optical thickness n*d = lambda0/4 for mirror layers establishes stopband
Curvature penalty prevents rapid thickness oscillations that break interference coherence
expected_advantages: Preserves proven mirror performance from iteration 02
Bounded search prevents optimizer divergence observed in iterations 09 and 13
Curvature penalty maintains physical layer continuity
±15nm bounds balance exploration freedom with stability
known_risks: May not exceed iteration 02 best score if cavity physics already optimized
Fixed front mirror may limit further stopband improvement
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 alternating stack on Fused Silica substrate for 1550nm bandpass filtering. Layers 1-8 (Ta2O5/SiO2 pairs) fixed at thicknesses [158.5, 268.4, 158.3, 268.2, 158.1, 268.0, 157.9, 267.9] nm from iteration 02 baseline. Layers 9-20 initialized at mean thickness from iterations 06, 13, and 17 candidates, optimized within ±15nm absolute bounds. Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with curvature penalty term penalizing |d[i+1] - 2*d[i] + d[i-1]| > 5nm. Evaluate transmittance at normal incidence, unpolarized. Score objectives: maximize mean T at 1550nm (weight 1.0), minimize mean T in 1400-1500nm (weight 0.5), minimize mean T in 1600-1700nm (weight 0.5). Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: ±15nm bounded perturbation on layers 8-19, re-initialization from iteration 02 baseline for layers 1-8, asymmetric half constrained to mean of last three candidates, curvature penalty added. Differs from iteration 17 which used ±20nm bounds without curvature penalty and from iteration 09 which used overly restrictive ±4nm bounds.
